Summary

Fixes from run r20261007-100412 — driver-item hold, harness pin on success, untracked archive-first, data-step lock, overlap default, report commit pointers — r20261010-134127

TL;DR

Nine serial groups closed the four seams the run-driver hit on infinity-skills run r20261007-100412, plus the smaller items from the same handoff. Every group completed; the only friction was two merge-gate failures on guard tests the plan did not list and one coder retired at the round cap.

  • All nine groups completed and the plugin reads 0.23.0; the facts count u9 as not landed only because its second item is unverified in the gen-2 report, while the bump commit ce73f5e2 is on the branch (g5-6)
  • Cost $10.42 across 13 sessions; g5 took 25 min and four sessions against 4–13 min and one or two sessions for every other group (g5/coder/gen1)
  • Driver items are now recorded and hold dependents, untracked leftovers archive on the first strike, the harness pin is written only after a green smoke and reset by retry, a run-level lock serialises driver data steps and the gate, and overlap is the default failure policy (orchestrator/execution/scheduler.py)

Problems found

Both gate failures and the retired coder trace back to the plan, not to the coders.

  • The plan's Files omitted an existing drift test that pins every EscalationKind to the UI union, so g4's gate failed the moment it added the new kind (006a7b155a75)
  • U11 depends on U2, so the unit that extends the enum landed before the unit that mirrors it; a unit extending a mirrored enum owns the mirror edit, or the mirror unit comes first (u11)
  • The plan's Files omitted the e2e stub test that pinned the old two-strike untracked ladder, so g6's gate failed on it (047184290ce2)
  • A required coder item "whole suite green" is unmeetable inside a confined worker: two baseline tests fail whenever pytest's basetemp sits inside the repo tree, which is every worker's TMPDIR, and the reviewer held g5's gate two rounds over it (tests/test_preflight_baseline.py)
  • The reviewer's third round found a bug the unit text missed: optimize's pin lives at groups/<gid>/eval/harness.sha256 and the retry reset only looked under run/eval/ (g5/reviewer/gen1)
  • The live harness-pin test asserted a manifest field that never existed: the artifact entry carries measurements only, never the record's kpi_value, threshold_cleared or harness_hash (tests/test_harness_pin_live.py)
  • Session hooks leave .codegraph/, .cursor/ and __pycache__/ untracked in every scratch worktree, and the first-strike ladder now archives them with an informational surprise on every live run (g1-8)

base-context.md (858 lines)

Base context

Worker ground rules

These rules apply to every coder and reviewer session forked from this base context, for the spec you will be given below and the plan document that follows it.

For coders

  • Work only inside your worktree (your current working directory); never touch paths outside it.
  • Your worktree owns its own environment: dependency changes require uv sync run inside the worktree, and any verification item that imports a new dependency must pass there, in that worktree — never against the parent checkout's environment. Always sync with the project's extras (uv sync --all-extras, or whatever the project's own instructions name): a plain uv sync strips the extras, the optional dependencies disappear from the venv, and tests that import them skip at module level — a green run that verified nothing.
  • Verification outputs, logs, and temporary scripts go in .coder-scratch/ at the root of your worktree — it is git-ignored for you and archived with the group's artifacts. Anything else left untracked in the worktree fails the merge gate: commit it, move it into .coder-scratch/, or delete it before you report.
  • Never write to /tmp (or /var/tmp, or mktemp with no directory) — not for scratch files, not for a quick check, not when a spec or a habit suggests it. /tmp is wiped on restart and lies outside the run's record, so whatever lands there is lost evidence. Your worktree already is the temporary space: .coder-scratch/ for throwaway files, mktemp -p .coder-scratch when a tool needs a unique path, and a data_dirs path for large outputs that must outlive the group.
  • Use git -C <absolute path> … instead of cd X && git …: the CLI refuses the compound command because the cd changes the trust boundary.
  • Never put $(…), brace expansion ({a,b}) or a newline followed by # inside a quoted argument — the CLI's static analysis refuses them (simple_expansion, "Newline followed by #"). Multi-line Python goes in a file under .coder-scratch/ that you then run, not in a python -c "…" argument.
  • Read the exact span before every Edit; copy old_string from that output, never from a diff or from memory.
  • Run long or real verification (a full suite, a pipeline over real data, a render) in the foreground and wait for it. A background task is killed when your session ends its turn, so a verification you backgrounded never finishes and its pass is a guess. One tool call is capped at 10 minutes: a single command that needs longer (a long render, a slow pipeline) cannot finish inside a call and cannot be backgrounded across your turn. Run what fits in parts (one chapter, one input, resuming from what is already on disk); if the step cannot be split, report it skipped with the exact command and its expected duration instead of relaunching it again.
  • Data and large binaries never go through git. Directories that appear in your worktree as symlinks (the run's shared data directories) are shared live with every other group and the integration tree: put downloads, models, corpora and generated media there and read inputs from there. Do not commit any file above ~50 MB; the orchestrator relocates such files out of git for you, but a symlink where you expected a file means exactly that happened. Those symlinks resolve outside your worktree, so ls/find on them is refused ("may only list files in the allowed working directories") — that refusal is not evidence the data is missing. List them with the Glob tool, read them with Read, and let the project's own commands open them; never report shared data absent on the strength of a refused ls.
  • Implement the spec you are given fully — code and tests — following the conventions established above.
  • Commit early and often: after each self-contained step that leaves the worktree in a consistent state (a finished file, a passing unit of work), make a git commit with a clear conventional message. Do not accumulate large uncommitted work — if your session is interrupted, only committed work survives; anything uncommitted is lost when the group restarts. The commit subject must start with the first character of the type, not whitespace — if you're using a heredoc to pass the message, check the exact bytes, since a leading newline or space before the subject line is a common heredoc mistake.
  • If a command is denied for permissions, retry the identical command up to three times total, then stop and report status permission_denied with the denied command verbatim in denied_command. Re-sending the identical command is not a workaround; alternate quoting, alternate spellings, shelling through another interpreter, and subprocess.run substitution for the same command are all banned — they route around the sandbox instead of reporting the block.
  • Verify your work against the verification items you will be given before reporting — for real. A verification item is pass only if you ran it in this worktree against the actual dependency, data, or service it names: a mock, a stub backend, a lazily-imported library that was never installed, or "the unit tests I wrote pass" does not make an item about that library pass. If you could not run an item for real, report it skipped with the reason in its notes — a skipped is honest and recoverable; a false pass is the single worst report you can make, because nothing downstream will ever look again. A DRIVER-RUN (sandbox-safe) item's skipped must name the exact command you ran and the error it produced — a bare driver-run note is not a reason.
  • Your environment is part of your work. If uv sync (with the project's extras) fails, or a dependency the spec relies on cannot be installed or imported in this worktree, first try to fix it (pin, alternative build, version constraint) and commit that fix. If you cannot make the real dependency work, do not design around it and report completed: report status blocked with the exact error in summary. The orchestrator resolves a blocked report (spec rewrite, or a human when one is configured); a silent completed on a fake environment resolves nothing.

For reviewers

  • Compute the diff yourself from git rather than trusting the coder's report: verify claims against the actual code and run the tests the spec calls for.
  • Check the environment before you check the code: confirm uv sync with the project's extras succeeds in this worktree and that every dependency the spec names actually imports here. Then check that at least one verification item exercised the real dependency, data, or service — not a mock or a stub. A report whose every pass rests on mocks of the thing under test is changes_required ("exercise the real X in item N"); a dependency that cannot be made to work at all in this environment is too_hard, stated plainly, never approved.
  • If you need scratch space, use only the directory the round names for it, and do not leave scratch files anywhere else in the worktree — the merge gate requires a clean tree.

Report block rules (both roles)

Every final message ends with EXACTLY ONE <run-report> block, whose body is valid JSON with no trailing commas and no comments, and nothing after the closing tag.

  • A coder's status attribute is one of completed | blocked | failed | needs_input | permission_denied and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • Use needs_input only when a decision only a human can make blocks you (an ambiguous requirement, a product trade-off, missing access). Put the single specific question in a top-level "question" field; the run pauses and resumes you with the operator's answer. Do not use it for anything you can resolve yourself.
    • Use permission_denied only after retrying the identical denied command up to three times total. Put the exact command in a top-level "denied_command" field, verbatim, with no paraphrasing or quoting changes. Do not use it for a blocked report — that status is unrelated to permission denials.
    • With permission_denied, also set two top-level fields that say how it was denied, because three unrelated causes look identical from where you stand and each needs a different fix from the operator:
      • "denial_error": the error text you actually saw, verbatim — do not summarize or rephrase it. If nothing came back at all, write exactly no error text was returned; a stated absence is usable, a blank field is not.
      • "denial_source": "tool_refused" if the tool call was refused and the command never ran, or "command_error" if the command ran and failed. You know which one happened and the orchestrator cannot work it out afterwards, so this is the single most useful thing you can report here.
    • Every verification item you were given must appear in "verification_results" with status pass | fail | skipped.
  • A reviewer's status attribute is one of approved | changes_required | too_hard | structural and must match the JSON body's "status" field.
    • approved: the work satisfies the spec and its verification items.
    • changes_required: fixable within this group — list concrete, actionable items in "required_changes".
    • too_hard: the spec cannot be satisfied by iterating here; escalate for a spec rewrite.
    • structural: the group boundaries themselves are wrong (work belongs to or conflicts with another group).
  • Either role may record a surprise: a finding that likely invalidates another group's assignment — an interface mismatch, a missing dependency, work that belongs elsewhere. Record it instead of fixing it yourself: {"kind": "interface_mismatch" | "missing_dependency" | "merge_conflict" | "other", "description": "...", "affected_groups": ["g2"]} Each affected_groups entry is one bare id — a plan task id (u8) or a group id (g2), nothing around it. Prefer the plan's task id when you are not sure which group owns the work. A finding that matters for later work but no group in this run (a defect worth a future round) takes "affected_groups": []; it is carried into the run's end-of-run report.

Repo conventions (CLAUDE.md)

smart-mcps

A Claude Code plugin that installs skills and session hooks for codegraph, NotebookLM, and Perplexity.

Plugin structure

This is a Claude Code plugin repository. Hooks and skills are distributed to plugin consumers via auto-discovered files:

Path Purpose
hooks/hooks.json Plugin-level hook registrations (uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT})
hooks/scripts/ Hook implementation scripts (.py and .sh)
skills/ Skill definitions
agents/ Subagent definitions (auto-discovered; .claude/agents symlinks here for local dev)
codegraph_mcp/ FastMCP proxy exposing 6 trimmed codegraph tools (smart-mcps-codegraph)
.mcp.json MCP server registration — serves plugin consumers and local dev (see below)
.claude-plugin/plugin.json Plugin identity (name, version)
.claude/settings.json Project-level hooks for local development (uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)

Adding hooks — always register in both places

Every hook script must be wired up in two files:

  1. hooks/hooks.json — so plugin consumers receive it. Uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.
  2. .claude/settings.json — so it runs locally during development. Uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

Matchers are case-sensitive and PascalCase in both files (e.g. "Edit|Write|MultiEdit", "Bash") — a lowercase matcher silently matches nothing. This applies to every event, including SessionStart (codegraph reindex, formatter bootstrap), not just PostToolUse.

Registering in only one place means either plugin consumers or local dev is broken. Always do both.

MCP servers — one file, not two

The dual-registration rule above does not apply to MCP servers: .claude/settings.json has no mcpServers key (it only approves servers via enabledMcpjsonServers). A single .mcp.json at the repo root covers both audiences, because Claude Code reads it twice:

  • Plugin consumers — auto-discovered as the plugin's ./.mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__plugin_smart-mcps_codegraph__<tool>.
  • Local dev — read as the project-scoped .mcp.json; tools resolve as mcp__codegraph__<tool>.

Hence "--project", "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}". ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is set only for consumers; locally it falls back to . (the server's cwd is the project root). Two constraints worth knowing before editing that line:

  • ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is not available in .mcp.json — only in hooks. Using it yields a "Missing environment variables" warning.
  • Defaults don't nest. ${VAR:-default} works, but ${A:-${B}} does not expand B — it silently passes a literal, which uv may accept when the console script is already on PATH, hiding the bug locally while breaking for consumers.

Never keep working notes in the /tmp scratchpad

The session scratchpad under /tmp is wiped when the Claude Code process restarts — not just at the end of a session. Anything written there is gone without warning.

This has already cost real work: on 2026-07-29 a restart destroyed the accumulated findings and deferred-fix list for two sessions of orchestrator debugging, plus a patch backup of a group's stranded work.

Use /tmp only for genuinely throwaway intermediates. Anything another session would want — findings, deferred-fix lists, handoff notes, backups of uncommitted work — goes somewhere durable:

what where
Run findings, deferred fixes, backups .orchestrator/ — gitignored, survives restarts, never collides with a group merge
Facts worth recalling across sessions the auto-memory dir (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/)
Anything the repo should carry docs/ — committed

Write it durably as you go, not at the end. A restart gives no notice.

In a remote container, only a pushed commit is durable

The table above assumes a local machine, where .orchestrator/ outlives the Claude Code process. In Claude Code on the web the repository lives in an ephemeral container that is reclaimed after inactivity, and .orchestrator/ is gitignored — so it is destroyed with the container, and so is the auto-memory directory. /tmp and .orchestrator/ are equally volatile there.

So when the session is a remote container, the table collapses to one row: anything worth keeping goes into docs/ and is committed and pushed. Use .orchestrator/ for genuinely throwaway intermediates only, and promote anything a later session would want — findings, research, handoff notes — into committed documents before the work is done. docs/research/ and docs/handoffs/ exist for exactly this.

Plan digest (2026-10-10-001-fix-run-r20261007-100412-seams-plan.md)

title: Fixes from run r20261007-100412 — driver-item hold, harness pin on success, untracked archive-first, data-step lock, overlap default, report commit pointers type: fix date: 2026-10-10 origin: docs/handoffs/2026-10-09-orchestrator-seams-from-run-r20261007-100412.md

Fixes from run r20261007-100412 — driver-item hold, harness pin on success, untracked archive-first, data-step lock, overlap default, report commit pointers

Objective

Close the four orchestrator seams the run-driver found driving infinity-skills run r20261007-100412 (handoff docs/handoffs/2026-10-09-orchestrator-seams-from-run-r20261007-100412.md, evidence in /home/gbm1996/wksp/infinity-skills/.orchestrator/notes-r20261007-100412.md and that run's logs/run.log), plus the smaller items from the same run, without adding any large feature:

  1. No window for a Run (driver): step between dependent groups — g16: completed at 10:26:14, g17 … researcher launching at 10:26:19 (run.log lines 789/794); g17 read a profile g16-3 had not rendered yet.
  2. Evaluate/optimize pin the harness hash before the smoke — g9's smoke failed (exit 2), the operator fixed the fixture, and retry died at 03:01:44 on harness path changed since the first evaluation.
  3. The untracked ladder's relaunch note invites rm -r — ESC 8146509c3bb2 timed out, the relaunched coder ran rm -r ./file:data, the allowlist denied it, the run halted overnight (run.log 469-478).
  4. A driver data step races a gate that reads the live data layer — the driver's ingest-sessions wrote data/corpus.db while g19's gate ran the server tests over it (ESC fedc4a348855).

Smaller items carried: report --scaffold lists the integration tip sha that moves once the one-pager is committed; an evaluate group's own harness command did not satisfy its Run (driver, sandbox-safe): item (g9-1, g11-1); the run-driver skill's "pending escalation" heuristic false-alarms on a timed-out request; on_group_failure defaults to halt, which cost a full retry + resume cycle on every designed fail-fast.

Out of scope (no action needed): the handoff's observation that g16's pre-launch spec rewrite consumed an upstream surprise and kept its verification item ids — that is the 0.21.1 fix working as intended.

Every seam gets a live-tier test (-m llm) that only a real run can prove; uv run pytest -q stays green; the plugin version bumps to 0.23.0 and the driver reinstalls the tool with --no-cache as the last driver item.

What we already know (resolved context)

  • Scheduler admission. Scheduler.run (orchestrator/execution/scheduler.py:522-595) recomputes _admissible() every cycle; _holds_on (scheduler.py:633-655) returns one GroupHold per reason from HoldReason (scheduler.py:150-156: DAG_DEPENDENCY, FAILURE_GATE, FILE_OVERLAP, RUN_HALTED); _unmet_deps (scheduler.py:597-604) treats COMPLETED and RESOLVED as met. When nothing is in flight and nothing is admissible, run() returns if the run is halted or every blocked group is reachable from a failure, else raises NoProgressError (scheduler.py:555-580) — a new hold kind that waits on the operator must be excluded from that wedge check. GroupRunState.holds (scheduler.py:171-180) is persisted and status prints it verbatim as holds: … (orchestrator/cli.py:3057); _record_holds writes it. The scheduler already owns self._broker / self._policy (scheduler.py:299-330) and raises GROUP_RESOLVE escalations itself from _resolve_failure; EscalationBroker.raise_escalation (orchestrator/execution/escalation.py:110-150) blocks on a worker thread, writes escalations/request-<id>.json, logs ESCALATION <id> [<kind>] <gid>: <prompt>, and returns None on timeout (logging ESCALATION <id> timed out → <action>, escalation.py:153-155). Tiers: _ON_FAILURE, _ON_STUCK, _INTERACTIVE (escalation.py:38-54); EscalationKind is orchestrator/model.py:469-487; HumanAction (model.py:490-499) is answer | retry | skip | abort. The Observatory mirrors the kinds in ui/src/types.ts:231-234 (a string union) and ui/src/components/EscalationPanel.tsx:25-28 (label map); hold reasons are not enumerated in the UI. The interactive-only GROUP_START gate is raised in orchestrator/execution/generation.py:190-192 (code recipe only — g17 was a research group, so the hold must live in the scheduler, not a ladder).
  • Driver items today. VerificationItem.driver_run / sandbox_safe (orchestrator/model.py:62-84) derive from the Run (driver): marker. MergeLadder._log_driver_run_items (orchestrator/execution/merge_ladder.py:80-128) logs N driver-run verification item(s) not run by the coder — <ids> from the latest coder report only. pending_driver_run_items (orchestrator/execution/finish.py:84-114) re-derives the same set from effective_group(paths, group).verification and latest_report(paths, gid) (orchestrator/execution/manifest.py:428-452, glob report-g*-r*.json); _maybe_auto_finish (orchestrator/cli.py:2483-2506) prints not auto-finishing — N driver-run verification item(s) wait for the run driver (<gid>: <ids>; …). Nothing records that the driver ran an item. orchestrator/execution/driver_items.py (3 KB) holds the driver_items_naming_missing_tests gate check and is the natural home for a record store. A run/evaluate/optimize group writes a synthetic RunVerificationReport (orchestrator/execution/run_executor.py:520-547) with one pass per item whose Run: command run_command_for_item (orchestrator/recipes/run.py:125-139) matches a declared command by whitespace-normalised equality — g9-1's item uv run python scripts/cause_class_harness.py --fixture data/eval/cause_fixture.json did not match the declared … --fixture data/eval/cause_fixture.json --out .coder-scratch/measurements.json, so it stayed pending (same for g11-1). _RUN_ITEM_RE (run.py:119-122) extracts the backticked or bare command after Run (…):.
  • Harness pin. EvaluateExecution._before_commands (orchestrator/execution/evaluate_executor.py:72-101) and OptimizeExecution._run_evaluation (orchestrator/execution/optimize_executor.py:518-545) compute _harness_snapshot/_combined_hash and, when <group_dir>/run/eval/harness.sha256 is absent, write it before _run_smoke; when present they compare and raise GroupFailure("… harness path changed since the first evaluation: <path>"). _run_smoke fails via _triage_and_fail (evaluate) or _EvalCrash (optimize). _eval_dir() is self._run_dir() / "eval". retry_group → _retry_failed (orchestrator/execution/retry.py:76-141) refreshes the branch, backs up state, resets the entry to PENDING and logs retried by operator — refreshed onto <integration>, reset to pending; it never touches run/eval/. Existing tests: tests/test_evaluate_recipe.py (7 KB; repo, make_group, make_deps, _run, base_args fixtures; test_editing_harness_between_attempts_fails_the_second_attempt_naming_it at line 152 pins today's behaviour and must be re-shaped, not deleted), tests/test_optimize_executor.py:340 (test_harness_edited_outside_the_loop_between_evaluations_fails_naming_the_path), tests/test_retry.py (15.6 KB; repo, make_group, setup-style helpers). docs/orchestrator-kpi-harness.md:41-43 says "hashed once, at first use".
  • Untracked ladder. run_preflight (orchestrator/execution/preflight.py:437-448) raises PreflightFailure(kind="untracked", paths=…) when the only dirt is ?? entries. MergeLadder._merge (merge_ladder.py:178-187) routes it to _handle_untracked (merge_ladder.py:349-398): strike 1 escalates PREFLIGHT_FAILED; retry with no text re-runs the gate; otherwise it relaunches a fresh coder with the note untracked files left in the worktree: <paths> — commit them, move them into .coder-scratch/, or delete them; strike 2 moves the paths with _move_paths (merge_ladder.py:565-580) into paths.untracked_archive_dir(gid) (manifest.py:259-262, groups/<gid>/untracked/), logs UNTRACKED FILES ARCHIVED …, spreads an informational surprise and continues the merge loop. _untracked_strikes is declared on merge_ladder.py:69, orchestrator/execution/host.py:53, initialised in orchestrator/execution/review.py:184, and listed in docs/orchestrator-flow.md:74. Tests: tests/test_merge_gate_triage.py:351-430 (_untracked, test_first_untracked_failure_relaunches_the_same_spec_with_a_note, test_second_consecutive_untracked_failure_archives_and_merges, test_untracked_failure_with_operator_retry_no_text_reruns_the_gate) on the scripted Harness/StubRunner rig from tests/test_review_loop.py (102 KB — never in Files). The run skill's table row (.claude/skills/orchestrator-run/SKILL.md:300) promises "untracked leftovers are handled for you (relaunch, then archive)".
  • Gate and data layer. IntegrationManager.merge_group (orchestrator/execution/merge.py:222-275) refreshes, checks commits_ahead, calls run_preflight(...) and merges, all under self._lock; it knows self.run_id and self.repo_root. materialize_data_layer (orchestrator/execution/worktrees.py:744-770) symlinks every [workspace] data_dirs entry into every worktree from the single copy under the repo root, so a driver write is visible to a running gate instantly. DriverLock (orchestrator/execution/driver.py:123, _open_lock_fd line 70, is_driving line 78) is the existing flock pattern; RunPaths (manifest.py:163-262) is the one place run-dir paths are spelled out. The run preflight summary line is printed at cli.py:2088 (on-failure …) and run <id>: on_group_failure=… is logged at cli.py:2160. The CLI runs under test as [sys.executable, "-m", "orchestrator.cli", …] from a tmp repo (tests/test_rewrite_counter.py:102-121) — the installed smart-mcps-orchestrate is a non-editable copy of main.
  • Failure policy. ExecutionConfig.on_group_failure: Literal["halt","overlap"] = "halt" (orchestrator/config.py:418-425); _halted_by (scheduler.py:507-518). Tests that assume the default is halt: tests/test_scheduler.py:872-1005 (five test_halt_* functions, 66 KB file — never in Files; they must pass ExecutionConfig(on_group_failure="halt") explicitly), tests/test_e2e_faults.py:485-520 (writes halt into the config and asserts the --on-failure overlap flag wins), tests/test_cli.py:1215-1239 (102 KB — never in Files; asserts the halt report's escape-hatch text, which stays correct: a halted run can only arise from an explicit --on-failure halt after the flip). CONTEXT.md:277-286 (Failure Policy) and docs/orchestrator-grouping-config.md:351 say halt is the default.
  • Report pointers. _valid_pointers (orchestrator/report/onepager.py:84-106) accepts base_sha[:8] and tip_sha[:8] from GitRangeFacts (orchestrator/report/facts.py:48-49); _resolve_git_range (facts.py:227-249) takes tip_sha from the pushed line in run.log or rev-parse of the integration branch — so the tip the scaffold lists moves the moment the driver commits the one-pager onto integration, and --validate (cli.py:3414-3421, same build_facts) then rejects it. tests/test_report_onepager.py (13 KB, make_facts() builds a RunFacts by hand) and tests/test_report_facts.py (14.7 KB).
  • Live tier. pytestmark = [pytest.mark.llm, skipif(no claude)]; excluded by addopts = -m "not llm" (pyproject.toml:65); tests/test_e2e_live.py:60-140 builds a session-scoped scratch repo with [session] confine = true, a hand-built groups.json + base-context.md under .orchestrator/groupings/plan/, and drives main(["run", …]); tests/test_run_recipe_live.py does the same for a run group ([recipes] enabled = ["run"]). A test that must act during a run launches the CLI as a subprocess and polls logs/run.log. run --run-id <id> refuses an existing run dir (cli.py:1915).
  • Versioning. .claude-plugin/plugin.json is 0.22.1; the convention is one chore(plugin): <version> — <summary> commit touching only that file (dc2d669). pyproject.toml stays 0.1.0 (never bumped). The installed tool is verified from outside the repo (a python -c check from inside the checkout lies — cwd is on sys.path).
  • Repo config. .orchestrator/config.toml here has no [workspace] data_dirs and no [recipes] block; this plan has only code units and reads no data files.

Decisions

  • The driver-item hold is a scheduler hold reason, recorded through a new driver-item subcommand, and surfaced as an escalation only when HITL is on. A group is held while a COMPLETED/RESOLVED dependency still carries a required Run (driver): item that neither the coder's latest report nor groups/<gid>/driver-items.json marks run; status shows the hold; the run log says how to release it. With [escalation] enabled and a tier that includes the new driver_items_pending kind (on_stuck, interactive), one request is raised per held group so the driver's Monitor fires; answer (any action but skip/abort) releases without recording, and a timeout releases too (today's behaviour). Alternatives rejected: an escalation-only gate (nothing is ever recorded, so auto-finish and status stay blind; a 4-hour timeout blocks a run with HITL off), and a wait_for_driver marker in the plan (one more thing a planner forgets).
  • The harness hash is pinned only after the smoke and the first scoring exit 0, and retry deletes the pin. The pin exists to catch a harness edited under a running loop; a failed smoke never scored anything, so there is nothing to protect. retry is the operator's explicit "I changed the world" — it removes run/eval/harness.sha256 and logs the old combined hash so the report can see the harness changed. Rejected: pin-on-success alone (a harness fixed after a successful first attempt still fails the retry), and retry-reset alone (a crash re-entry after a failed smoke keeps the stale pin).
  • The untracked ladder archives on the first strike and merges; it never relaunches on its own. The escalation stays (on_stuck): retry with no text re-runs the gate, retry with text is the operator's explicit relaunch (the note names git mv … .coder-scratch/ and never "delete"). Every other outcome (timeout, autonomous, answer) moves the paths to groups/<gid>/untracked/, spreads the informational surprise, re-runs the gate and merges. Rejected: moving leftovers into .coder-scratch/ and relaunching (one generation on every probe artifact; the only observed strikes were probe artifacts, and recipe groups' forgotten outputs are already caught by _commit_declared_outputs / "no commits ahead").
  • The gate and driver data steps exclude each other through one run-level flock, data-step.lock, with a data-step wrapper the driver uses. merge_group holds it around run_preflight; smart-mcps-orchestrate data-step <run> -- <cmd> holds it around the command; whichever side waits logs why. A launch-time warning names the wrapper whenever data_dirs is configured. Rejected: warning only (the race stays on the driver's attention, which lapsed twice in that run).
  • on_group_failure defaults to overlap. Every designed fail-fast (census bar, unreviewed fixture) under halt cost a retry + resume cycle and a new driver process; overlap still strands dependents and file-overlapping groups. --on-failure halt remains the escape hatch, and the halt report's advice text stays correct because a halted run now only arises from an explicit halt. Rejected: keep halt and document (the user chose the flip).
  • A run-group item is satisfied by a declared command whose argv starts with the item's Run: argv. Exact equality missed g9-1/g11-1 because the recipe adds --out <measurements>. A prefix is the smallest rule that passes those and still rejects the --smoke item (its extra flag is not in the declared command).
  • One-pager commit pointers validate against every commit in base..tip, not just the two endpoints. GitRangeFacts gains the 8-character prefixes of git rev-list base..tip plus base.
  • Live tests are one file per seam. Four files sharing one module would pull four units into one group by file affinity; each unit owns its own tests/test_<seam>_live.py, run by the driver (-m llm).
  • No ADR. Every decision above is a one-line default or a mechanism a later plan can replace without migration.

Unit summaries

  • U1 (driver-item-record — the Driver Item Record: record_driver_item writes an item's outcome, auto-finish reads it, and a run group's own command satisfies a prefix-matching item) Summary: Ships groups/<gid>/driver-items.json behind two functions in orchestrator/execution/driver_items.py — record_driver_item(paths, group, item_id, status, notes) and pending_driver_items(paths, group) — that pending_driver_run_items (auto-finish) delegates to, plus a prefix rule in run_command_for_item so an evaluate/run group's declared command marks an item passed when its argv starts with the item's Run: argv; the CLI wiring is U10's.
  • U2 (driver-items-hold — the scheduler holds a dependent group while a dependency carries unrecorded driver items, and tells the driver how to release it) Summary: Adds HoldReason.DRIVER_ITEMS and EscalationKind.DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING (tiers on_stuck and interactive; the Observatory mirror is U11's): a group whose COMPLETED/RESOLVED dependency still has pending_driver_items is not admitted; the scheduler waits (never NoProgressError) and, with HITL on, raises one driver_items_pending request per such dependency that any answer/retry, a timeout, or recording its last pending item releases for every dependent at once.
  • U3 (harness-pin-on-success — evaluate/optimize pin the harness hash only after a successful smoke and first scoring; retry resets the pin) Summary: EvaluateExecution and OptimizeExecution compare against run/eval/harness.sha256 when it exists but write it only once the smoke and the first scoring command exit 0, and retry_group deletes the pin logging the old combined hash — so a fixture fixed after a failed smoke passes retry, while a harness edited under a running loop still fails naming the path.
  • U4 (untracked-archive-first — the merge gate archives untracked leftovers on the first strike and merges; no relaunch unless the operator asks) Summary: _handle_untracked escalates as today, then archives the untracked paths to groups/<gid>/untracked/, spreads the informational surprise and re-runs the gate on timeout, autonomous or answer; only retry --text relaunches, with a note that says git mv … .coder-scratch/ and never "delete"; _untracked_strikes is removed from the ladder, the host and the flow doc.
  • U5 (data-step-lock — the gate and driver data steps exclude each other through data-step.lock, held by the gate and by run_data_step) Summary: Adds orchestrator/execution/data_step.py (a run-level flock at <run_dir>/data-step.lock, hold_data_step_lock(paths, label, log) and run_data_step(repo_root, run_id, cmd) -> int) and wraps run_preflight in merge_group with it, so a driver data step and a merge gate never overlap; the data-step CLI wrapper and the launch-time warning are U10's.
  • U6 (overlap-default — on_group_failure defaults to overlap) Summary: Flips ExecutionConfig.on_group_failure to "overlap" and updates every test that silently relied on halt being the default, the grouping-config doc line, and the config docstring; --on-failure halt stays the escape hatch.
  • U7 (report-commit-pointers — one-pager pointers accept every commit in the run's range) Summary: GitRangeFacts carries commits (8-character prefixes of git rev-list base..tip plus base, oldest first) and _valid_pointers accepts them, so a scaffold written before the one-pager commit still validates after it.
  • U8 (run-skill-and-docs — the run-driver skill, the flow doc and the glossary describe the new hold, record, data step, untracked outcome and failure default) Summary: Rewrites the run-driver skill's affected rows and phases (Monitor rule for a timed-out request, the untracked row, driver-item and data-step usage, --on-failure guidance, the held — dependency anchor), adds driver-item and data-step to docs/orchestrator-flow.md §7, and adds Driver Item Record and Data Step to CONTEXT.md while correcting Failure Policy.
  • U9 (version-bump — plugin 0.22.1 → 0.23.0 and the reinstall the driver verifies from outside the repo) Summary: Bumps .claude-plugin/plugin.json to 0.23.0 in a one-file chore(plugin): 0.23.0 — … commit once every other unit has merged; the driver reinstalls the tool with --no-cache and proves the new subcommands are on PATH from outside the checkout.
  • U10 (cli-subcommands — driver-item and data-step on the CLI, the status subcommand's driver-item lines, and the launch-time data-layer warning) Summary: Wires smart-mcps-orchestrate driver-item <run> <gid> <item_id> --status pass|fail|skipped [--notes …|--notes-file …] [--repo] and smart-mcps-orchestrate data-step <run> [--repo] -- <cmd…> into orchestrator/cli.py as thin wrappers over U1's record_driver_item and U5's run_data_step, prints recorded driver items in the status subcommand's group block, and logs U5's data_dirs_gate_warning text in the run preflight.
  • U11 (observatory-kind-mirror — the Observatory lists driver_items_pending and a drift test pins every escalation kind to the UI union) Summary: Adds driver_items_pending to the Observatory's escalation-kind union and label map and a test that fails whenever a Python EscalationKind value is missing from ui/src/types.ts, so the next new kind cannot drift silently.

  • U2 consumes: driver-items.json
  • U5 implements: data-step.lock
  • U10 consumes: driver-items.json, data-step.lock

U1. driver-item-record — the Driver Item Record: record_driver_item writes an item's outcome, auto-finish reads it, and a run group's own command satisfies a prefix-matching item

  • Summary: Ships groups/<gid>/driver-items.json behind two functions in orchestrator/execution/driver_items.py — record_driver_item(paths, group, item_id, status, notes) and pending_driver_items(paths, group) — that pending_driver_run_items (auto-finish) delegates to, plus a prefix rule in run_command_for_item so an evaluate/run group's declared command marks an item passed when its argv starts with the item's Run: argv; the CLI wiring is U10's.

Plan section U5

U5. data-step-lock — the gate and driver data steps exclude each other through data-step.lock, held by the gate and by run_data_step

  • Summary: Adds orchestrator/execution/data_step.py (a run-level flock at <run_dir>/data-step.lock, hold_data_step_lock(paths, label, log) and run_data_step(repo_root, run_id, cmd) -> int) and wraps run_preflight in merge_group with it, so a driver data step and a merge gate never overlap; the data-step CLI wrapper and the launch-time warning are U10's.
  • Goal: The gate's check never runs while a driver data step runs, and a data step never starts while a gate runs. run_data_step writes <run_dir>/data-step.json {cmd, pid, started_at} while it holds the lock, logs data step started: <cmd> and data step finished (exit N): <cmd> to run.log, runs the command with sh -c in the repo root with stdout/stderr passed through, removes the JSON, and returns the command's exit status. merge_group acquires the lock around run_preflight; if it is not immediately available it logs group <gid>: gate waiting for driver data step (<cmd from data-step.json>) once, then blocks with no upper bound, logging group <gid>: gate still waiting for driver data step (<cmd>, <age>) every DATA_STEP_REMINDER_S = 300 seconds until the lock is free. run_data_step mirrors: data step waiting for the merge gate once. RunPaths gains data_step_lock_path and data_step_record_path. data_dirs_gate_warning(workspace_config, run_id) -> str | None returns the text U10 logs at launch (data layer: [workspace] data_dirs <dirs> are read live by the merge gate — run every driver data step through: smart-mcps-orchestrate data-step <run> -- <cmd>) when the workspace config lists data dirs, else None.

  • Edge cases: a data step killed while holding the lock releases it (the kernel drops the flock), its stale data-step.json is overwritten by the next step and ignored by a gate that acquires the lock at once; the gate wait is unbounded by decision (a multi-hour ingest holds every merge for its whole duration)

orchestrator/execution/data_step.py
@@ -0,0 +1,138 @@
1"""Mutual exclusion between the merge gate and driver data steps.
2
3``[workspace] data_dirs`` are symlinked into every worktree from the single copy
4under the repo root, so a driver step that writes ``data/corpus.db`` is visible
5to a gate running the server tests over it instantly (r20261007-100412, ESC
6fedc4a348855). One run-level ``flock`` — ``<run_dir>/data-step.lock`` — is held
7by ``merge_group`` around the preflight and by ``run_data_step`` around the
8driver's command, so the two never overlap. The kernel drops an ``flock`` on any
9process death, so a killed data step cannot wedge the gate.
10"""
11
12from __future__ import annotations
13
14import contextlib
15import fcntl
16import json
17import os
18import subprocess
19import time
20from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
21from pathlib import Path
22
23from orchestrator.config import WorkspaceConfig
24from orchestrator.execution.manifest import RunPaths, atomic_write_text, log_event
25
26#: Seconds between "still waiting" lines. Module-level so a test can shrink it.
27DATA_STEP_REMINDER_S = 300
28_POLL_S = 0.1
29
30
31def _now() -> float:
32 return time.time()
33
34
35def _record_cmd(paths: RunPaths) -> str:
36 try:
37 payload = json.loads(paths.data_step_record_path.read_text())
38 except (OSError, ValueError):
39 return "unknown step"
40 cmd = payload.get("cmd") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
41 return str(cmd) if cmd else "unknown step"
42
43
44def _format_age(seconds: float) -> str:
45 seconds = int(seconds)
46 if seconds < 60:
47 return f"{seconds}s"
48 if seconds < 3600:
49 return f"{seconds // 60}m{seconds % 60:02d}s"
50 return f"{seconds // 3600}h{(seconds % 3600) // 60:02d}m"
51
52
53@contextlib.contextmanager
54def _locked(
55 paths: RunPaths,
56 on_wait: Callable[[], None],
57 on_remind: Callable[[float], None],
58) -> Iterator[None]:
59 """Hold the exclusive lock; call ``on_wait`` once if it is not free at once
60 and ``on_remind(age_s)`` every ``DATA_STEP_REMINDER_S`` until it is. No upper
61 bound on the wait, by decision."""
62 path = paths.data_step_lock_path
63 path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
64 # O_CLOEXEC: a child process must not inherit (and so keep holding) the lock.
65 fd = os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR | os.O_CLOEXEC, 0o644)
66 try:
67 try:
68 fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
69 except OSError:
70 on_wait()
71 started = last_reminder = time.monotonic()
72 while True:
73 try:
74 fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
75 break
76 except OSError:
77 time.sleep(_POLL_S)
78 now = time.monotonic()
79 if now - last_reminder >= DATA_STEP_REMINDER_S:
80 last_reminder = now
81 on_remind(now - started)
82 yield
83 finally:
84 os.close(fd) # closing the fd releases the flock
85
86
87@contextlib.contextmanager
88def hold_data_step_lock(paths: RunPaths, label: str, log: Callable[[str], None]) -> Iterator[None]:
89 """Held by the merge gate around its checks. ``label`` prefixes the log
90 lines (``group g3: gate``)."""
91
92 def _wait() -> None:
93 log(f"{label} waiting for driver data step ({_record_cmd(paths)})")
94
95 def _remind(age: float) -> None:
96 log(
97 f"{label} still waiting for driver data step ({_record_cmd(paths)}, {_format_age(age)})"
98 )
99
100 with _locked(paths, _wait, _remind):
101 yield
102
103
104def run_data_step(repo_root: Path, run_id: str, cmd: str) -> int:
105 """Run ``cmd`` (``sh -c``, in the repo root, output passed through) while
106 holding the data-step lock; returns the command's exit status."""
107 paths = RunPaths(repo_root, run_id)
108
109 def log(text: str) -> None:
110 log_event(paths, text)
111
112 with _locked(
113 paths,
114 lambda: log("data step waiting for the merge gate"),
115 lambda age: log(f"data step still waiting for the merge gate ({_format_age(age)})"),
116 ):
117 atomic_write_text(
118 paths.data_step_record_path,
119 json.dumps({"cmd": cmd, "pid": os.getpid(), "started_at": _now()}) + "\n",
120 )
121 log(f"data step started: {cmd}")
122 try:
123 code = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", cmd], cwd=repo_root, check=False).returncode
124 finally:
125 paths.data_step_record_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
126 log(f"data step finished (exit {code}): {cmd}")
127 return code
128
129
130def data_dirs_gate_warning(workspace: WorkspaceConfig | None, run_id: str) -> str | None:
131 """The launch-time warning when data dirs are shared live with the gate."""
132 if workspace is None or not workspace.data_dirs:

27DRIVER_ITEM_STATUSES = ("pass", "fail", "skipped")

30class DriverItemError(ValueError):
31 """The driver recorded an item the group's spec does not have, or a status
32 outside ``pass|fail|skipped``."""
33

35def read_driver_items(paths: RunPaths, group_id: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
36 """The driver's recorded outcomes for a group, ``{}`` when absent or unreadable."""
37 try:
38 payload = json.loads(paths.driver_items_path(group_id).read_text())
39 except (OSError, ValueError):
40 return {}
41 return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}

43
44def record_driver_item(
45 paths: RunPaths, group: Group, item_id: str, status: str, notes: str = ""
46) -> None:
47 """Write (or overwrite) the driver's outcome for one ``Run (driver):`` item.
48
49 The id is validated against the spec in force, so a typo cannot silently
50 "settle" nothing. A recorded ``fail`` stays pending in
51 ``pending_driver_items``; ``pass`` and ``skipped`` settle the item."""
52 known = [item.id for item in effective_group(paths, group).verification]
53 if item_id not in known:
54 raise DriverItemError(
55 f"group {group.id} has no verification item {item_id!r}; known ids: {', '.join(known)}"
56 )
57 if status not in DRIVER_ITEM_STATUSES:
58 raise DriverItemError(f"status {status!r} is not one of {', '.join(DRIVER_ITEM_STATUSES)}")
59 records = read_driver_items(paths, group.id)
60 records[item_id] = {
61 "status": status,
62 "notes": notes,
63 "recorded_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
64 "by": "driver",
65 }
66 atomic_write_text(paths.driver_items_path(group.id), json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
67 log_event(paths, f"group {group.id}: driver item {item_id} recorded {status} by the driver")
68
69
70def pending_driver_items(paths: RunPaths, group: Group) -> list[str]:
71 """Required ``driver_run`` items of the group's spec in force that neither
72 the coder's latest report passed nor the driver recorded ``pass``/``skipped``."""
73 report = latest_report(paths, group.id)
74 settled = {
75 r.get("item_id")
76 for r in (report.get("verification_results") if report else None) or []
77 if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("status") == "pass"
78 }
79 settled |= {
80 item_id
81 for item_id, record in read_driver_items(paths, group.id).items()
82 if isinstance(record, dict) and record.get("status") in ("pass", "skipped")
83 }
84 return [
85 item.id
86 for item in effective_group(paths, group).verification
87 if item.driver_run and item.required and item.id not in settled
88 ]

1"""The data-step lock: the merge gate and driver data steps never overlap."""
2
3from __future__ import annotations
4
5import subprocess
6import sys
7import threading
8import time
9
10import pytest
11
12from orchestrator.config import WorkspaceConfig
13from orchestrator.execution import data_step
14from orchestrator.execution.data_step import (
15 data_dirs_gate_warning,
16 hold_data_step_lock,
17 run_data_step,
18)

21RUN = "r-ds"
22
23
24def _spawn_step(repo, cmd: str) -> subprocess.Popen:
25 code = (
26 "import sys; from pathlib import Path; "
27 "from orchestrator.execution.data_step import run_data_step; "
28 f"sys.exit(run_data_step(Path(sys.argv[1]), {RUN!r}, sys.argv[2]))"
29 )
30 return subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code, str(repo), cmd])
31
32
33def _wait_for(predicate, timeout=10.0):
34 deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
35 while time.monotonic() < deadline:
36 if predicate():
37 return
38 time.sleep(0.05)
39 raise AssertionError("timed out")
40
41
42def test_gate_blocks_until_a_running_data_step_ends(tmp_path):
43 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, RUN)
44 proc = _spawn_step(tmp_path, "sleep 2")
45 try:
46 _wait_for(paths.data_step_record_path.is_file)
47 lines: list[str] = []
48 started = time.monotonic()
49 with hold_data_step_lock(paths, "group g1: gate", lines.append):
50 assert time.monotonic() - started >= 1.0
51 assert proc.wait(timeout=10) == 0
52 finally:
53 proc.kill()
54 waits = [line for line in lines if "still" not in line]
55 assert waits == ["group g1: gate waiting for driver data step (sleep 2)"]
56 assert not paths.data_step_record_path.exists()
57 log = paths.event_log_path.read_text()
58 assert "data step started: sleep 2" in log
59 assert "data step finished (exit 0): sleep 2" in log
60
61
62def test_data_step_blocks_while_the_gate_holds_the_lock(tmp_path):
63 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, RUN)
64 result: list[int] = []
65 with hold_data_step_lock(paths, "group g1: gate", lambda _t: None):
66 thread = threading.Thread(
67 target=lambda: result.append(run_data_step(tmp_path, RUN, "true"))
68 )
69 thread.start()
70 _wait_for(
71 lambda: (
72 paths.event_log_path.is_file()
73 and "data step waiting for the merge gate" in paths.event_log_path.read_text()
74 )
75 )
76 assert result == []
77 assert not paths.data_step_record_path.exists()
78 thread.join(timeout=10)
79 assert result == [0]
80 assert paths.event_log_path.read_text().count("data step waiting for the merge gate") == 1
81
82
83def test_record_is_present_during_the_step_and_exit_status_is_returned(tmp_path):
84 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, RUN)
85 seen: list[bool] = []
86 probe = f"test -f {paths.data_step_record_path}"
87 assert run_data_step(tmp_path, RUN, probe) == 0
88 assert run_data_step(tmp_path, RUN, "exit 3") == 3
89 assert not paths.data_step_record_path.exists()
90 assert "data step finished (exit 3): exit 3" in paths.event_log_path.read_text()
91 assert seen == []
92
93
94def test_reminder_repeats_while_the_lock_is_held(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
95 monkeypatch.setattr(data_step, "DATA_STEP_REMINDER_S", 0.2)
96 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, RUN)

99 _wait_for(paths.data_step_record_path.is_file)
100 lines: list[str] = []
101 with hold_data_step_lock(paths, "group g1: gate", lines.append):
102 pass
103 finally:
104 proc.kill()
105 first = [line for line in lines if "still waiting" not in line]
106 reminders = [line for line in lines if "still waiting" in line]
107 assert len(first) == 1
108 assert len(reminders) >= 2
109 assert all("sleep 1.5" in line for line in reminders)
110

112def test_a_killed_data_step_releases_the_lock(tmp_path):

@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
1"""A real confined run whose merge gate meets a driver data step.
2
3**This tier spends real tokens** (one tiny coder group) and is excluded from a
4plain `pytest` by `addopts = -m "not llm"`; opt in with `-m llm`. The run is a
5subprocess so the test can act *during* it: once the group's worktree exists it
6starts a data step that holds `data-step.lock`, waits for the gate to report it
7is blocked, then kills the step — the kernel drops the flock and the group must
8merge.
9"""
10
11from __future__ import annotations
12
13import os
14import shutil
15import signal
16import subprocess
17import sys
18import time
19from pathlib import Path
20
21import pytest
22
23from orchestrator.execution.manifest import RunPaths
24from orchestrator.grouping.pipeline import serialize_grouping
25from orchestrator.model import Group, GroupingResult, ReviewIntensity, VerificationItem
26
27pytestmark = [
28 pytest.mark.llm,
29 pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("claude") is None, reason="claude CLI not on PATH"),
30]
31
32RUN_ID = "live-ds"
33RUN_TIMEOUT_S = 900.0
34PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
35
36
37def _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
38 done = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
39 assert done.returncode == 0, f"git {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr}"
40 return done.stdout
41
42
43def _build_repo(root: Path) -> Path:
44 repo = root / "repo"
45 repo.mkdir()
46 _git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
47 _git(repo, "config", "user.email", "live@test")
48 _git(repo, "config", "user.name", "live")
49 (repo / "greeting.py").write_text('def greet():\n return "hello"\n')
50 (repo / "plan.md").write_text("# plan\n\n## Tasks\n\n- T1: add farewell()\n")
51 _git(repo, "add", "-A")
52 _git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "init")
53 (repo / ".orchestrator").mkdir()
54 (repo / ".orchestrator" / "config.toml").write_text(
55 "[session]\nconfine = true\n\n[escalation]\nenabled = false\n"
56 )
57 group = Group(
58 id="g1",
59 name="farewell",
60 summary="Add a farewell function.",
61 spec=(
62 'In greeting.py, add `farewell()` returning "goodbye" right after `greet()`. '
63 "Commit the change. Do not change anything else."
64 ),
65 difficulty=0.1,
66 intensity=ReviewIntensity.SELF_VERIFY,
67 files=["greeting.py"],
68 verification=[VerificationItem(id="v1", description="farewell() returns goodbye")],
69 )
70 grouping = repo / ".orchestrator" / "groupings" / "plan"
71 grouping.mkdir(parents=True)
72 (grouping / "groups.json").write_text(
73 serialize_grouping(GroupingResult(plan_path="plan.md", groups=[group]))
74 )
75 (grouping / "base-context.md").write_text("A tiny scratch repo. Keep every change minimal.\n")
76 return repo
77
78
79def _wait_for_log(log: Path, needle: str, deadline: float) -> None:
80 while time.monotonic() < deadline:
81 if log.is_file() and needle in log.read_text():
82 return
83 time.sleep(0.5)
84 tail = log.read_text()[-3000:] if log.is_file() else "(no run.log)"
85 raise AssertionError(f"never saw {needle!r} in run.log\n{tail}")
86
87
88def test_the_gate_waits_for_a_driver_data_step_then_merges(tmp_path):
89 repo = _build_repo(tmp_path)
90 paths = RunPaths(repo, RUN_ID)
91 env = {
92 **os.environ,
93 "PYTHONPATH": f"{PROJECT_ROOT}{os.pathsep}{os.environ.get('PYTHONPATH', '')}",
94 }
95 deadline = time.monotonic() + RUN_TIMEOUT_S
96 run = subprocess.Popen(
97 [
98 sys.executable, "-m", "orchestrator.cli", "run",
99 "--repo", str(repo), "--run-id", RUN_ID, "--intensity", "autonomous",
100 ],
101 cwd=repo,
102 env=env,
103 stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
104 stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
105 ) # fmt: skip
106 step = None
107 try:
108 _wait_for_log(paths.event_log_path, "worktree ready", deadline)
109 step_code = (
110 "import sys; from pathlib import Path; "
111 "from orchestrator.execution.data_step import run_data_step; "
112 f"sys.exit(run_data_step(Path(sys.argv[1]), {RUN_ID!r}, 'sleep 600'))"
113 )
114 step = subprocess.Popen(
115 [sys.executable, "-c", step_code, str(repo)],
116 env=env,
117 start_new_session=True,
118 )
119 _wait_for_log(
120 paths.event_log_path,
121 "gate waiting for driver data step (sleep 600)",
122 deadline,
123 )
124 os.killpg(step.pid, signal.SIGKILL) # the sleep child goes too
125 step.wait()
126 remaining = max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 1.0)
127 assert run.wait(timeout=remaining) == 0, paths.event_log_path.read_text()[-3000:]
128 finally:
129 if step is not None and step.poll() is None:
130 os.killpg(step.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
131 if run.poll() is None:
132 run.kill()
133 assert f"merge({RUN_ID}): g1" in _git(repo, "log", "--oneline", f"orchestrator/run-{RUN_ID}")

50def test_pass_and_skipped_settle_an_item_and_fail_keeps_it_pending(run):

g2: cli-subcommands — `driver-item` and `data-step` on the CLI, the status subcommand's driver-item lines, and the launch-time data-layer warning

u10: Wires `smart-mcps-orchestrate driver-item <run> <gid> <item_id> --status pass|fail|skipped [--notes …|--notes-file …] [--repo]` and `smart-mcps-orchestrate data-step <run> [--repo] -- <cmd…>` into `orchestrator/cli.py` as thin wrappers over U1's `record_driver_item` and U5's `run_data_step`, prints recorded driver items in the status subcommand's group block, and logs U5's `data_dirs_gate_warning` text in the run preflight.

Plan section U10

U10. cli-subcommands — driver-item and data-step on the CLI, the status subcommand's driver-item lines, and the launch-time data-layer warning

  • Summary: Wires smart-mcps-orchestrate driver-item <run> <gid> <item_id> --status pass|fail|skipped [--notes …|--notes-file …] [--repo] and smart-mcps-orchestrate data-step <run> [--repo] -- <cmd…> into orchestrator/cli.py as thin wrappers over U1's record_driver_item and U5's run_data_step, prints recorded driver items in the status subcommand's group block, and logs U5's data_dirs_gate_warning text in the run preflight.
  • Goal: driver-item resolves --repo, builds RunPaths, finds the group through groups.json + effective_group, calls record_driver_item, prints recorded <item_id> <status> for <gid> and exits 0; a DriverItemError prints error: … and exits 1; --notes-file - reads stdin exactly as answer --text-file - does. data-step takes the remainder after -- (argparse.REMAINDER), re-quotes it with shlex.join into the one shell string run_data_step takes (so -- sh -c 'sleep 600' survives as sh -c 'sleep 600'), runs it in the caller's current directory (never forced to the repo root — the driver runs data steps from the integration worktree), records that directory as cwd in data-step.json, and exits with the command's status; an empty remainder is a usage error (exit 2). The status subcommand's per-group block prints one driver items: <id> <status>[, …] line when the record file holds entries. _cmd_run logs the warning text right after the run <id>: on_group_failure=… line when it is not None. The dispatch chain in main gains both commands.
  • Recipe: —
  • Files: orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_cli_driver_steps.py (new, medium)
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U1, U5
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: consumes driver-items.json, data-step.lock
  • Verification:
    • Subprocess CLI tests against a tmp run dir (the tests/test_rewrite_counter.py:102-121 pattern): driver-item … --status pass writes groups/<gid>/driver-items.json and exits 0; an unknown item exits 1 naming the known ids; data-step <run> -- sh -c 'exit 3' exits 3 and run.log carries data step started / finished (exit 3); the status subcommand prints driver items: g1-2 pass after a record. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_cli_driver_steps.py -q Pass: green.
    • Both help texts exist. Run: uv run python -m orchestrator.cli driver-item --help Pass: exit 0 listing --status, --notes, --notes-file.
    • Run: uv run python -m orchestrator.cli data-step --help Pass: exit 0 showing the run id and the command remainder.
    • External oracle: a stub-tier run with [workspace] data_dirs = ["data"] in its config logs the data layer: … are read live by the merge gate line once, and a run without the block logs it never. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_cli_driver_steps.py -q -k warning Pass: green.
    • The CLI suite is otherwise unchanged. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py -q Pass: green.
    • Quoting and cwd survive the wrapper. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_cli_driver_steps.py -q -k quoting Pass: invoking data-step <run> -- sh -c 'exit 3' from a subdirectory of the tmp repo leaves run.log with data step finished (exit 3): sh -c 'exit 3' and, while it runs, data-step.json carries cmd equal to sh -c 'exit 3' and cwd equal to that subdirectory.
  • Edge cases: the command runs where the driver invoked the wrapper (--repo only locates the run dir); quoting inside the remainder is preserved by shlex.join; an empty remainder exits 2 before touching the lock
  • Non-goals / must-not: no new flags on run/resume; the subcommands never touch state.json. <!-- deepened 2026-10-10 from plan sha256:a8f26a9314dc -->

3300 """Record the driver's outcome for one ``Run (driver):`` item."""

3304 try:
3305 notes = sys.stdin.read() if str(args.notes_file) == "-" else args.notes_file.read_text()
3306 except OSError as exc:
3307 print(f"error: cannot read --notes-file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
3308 return 1

3310 print(f"error: no run grouping at {paths.groups_path}", file=sys.stderr)
3311 return 1
3312 grouping = GroupingResult.model_validate_json(paths.groups_path.read_text())
3313 group = next((g for g in grouping.groups if g.id == args.group_id), None)
3314 if group is None:
3315 known = ", ".join(g.id for g in grouping.groups)
3316 print(
3317 f"error: run {args.run_id} has no group {args.group_id!r}; known: {known}",
3318 file=sys.stderr,
3319 )

3321 try:
3322 record_driver_item(paths, group, args.item_id, args.status, notes)
3323 except DriverItemError as exc:

3325 return 1

3327 return 0

g4: driver-items-hold — the scheduler holds a dependent group while a dependency carries unrecorded driver items, and tells the driver how to release it

u2: Adds `HoldReason.DRIVER_ITEMS` and `EscalationKind.DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING` (tiers `on_stuck` and `interactive`; the Observatory mirror is U11's): a group whose COMPLETED/RESOLVED dependency still has `pending_driver_items` is not admitted; the scheduler waits (never `NoProgressError`) and, with HITL on, raises one `driver_items_pending` request per such dependency that any `answer`/`retry`, a timeout, or recording its last pending item releases for every dependent at once.

Plan section U2

U2. driver-items-hold — the scheduler holds a dependent group while a dependency carries unrecorded driver items, and tells the driver how to release it

  • Summary: Adds HoldReason.DRIVER_ITEMS and EscalationKind.DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING (tiers on_stuck and interactive; the Observatory mirror is U11's): a group whose COMPLETED/RESOLVED dependency still has pending_driver_items is not admitted; the scheduler waits (never NoProgressError) and, with HITL on, raises one driver_items_pending request per such dependency that any answer/retry, a timeout, or recording its last pending item releases for every dependent at once.
  • Goal: In _holds_on, after the DAG holds, every met dependency with non-empty pending_driver_items(paths, dep_group) contributes GroupHold(reason=DRIVER_ITEMS, group_id=dep, files=[<item ids>]) unless <run_dir>/groups/<dep>/driver-hold-released.json exists (written when that dependency's escalation is answered or times out). RESOLVED dependencies hold exactly like COMPLETED ones — their work is on integration and the driver items are its only live check; the driver records skipped with a reason to release a moot one. The first time a dependency holds anything the scheduler logs group <gid>: held — dependency <dep> has N driver-run item(s) unrecorded (<ids>); record them with smart-mcps-orchestrate driver-item <run> <dep> <id> --status … (one line per held group) and, when self._broker/self._policy escalate DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING, raises one request per dependency from a worker thread — group_id = the dependency, prompt = its unrecorded items and every group it is holding — never one per dependent; the response or timeout writes the release file, and a driver-item record that empties pending_driver_items releases the dependents on the next admission pass with no answer at all. In run(), when nothing is in flight and every blocked group's holds are only DRIVER_ITEMS (or DAG holds on such groups), the loop sleeps DRIVER_ITEMS_POLL_S = 5.0 and re-runs admission instead of raising NoProgressError or returning. The status subcommand already prints the hold verbatim. Hold evaluation must be cheap: pending_driver_items for a dependency is read once per admission pass, not per dependent.

  • Symbols: —

  • Verification:
    • In-process: g2 depends on g1; g1's spec carries a required driver-marked item; a completing executor finishes g1; without a record g2 stays PENDING with a driver_items hold naming g1 and the item id, the run.log carries the held — dependency g1 … line exactly once, and Scheduler.run() returns after the test writes the record (via driver_items module API) — no NoProgressError. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_driver_items_hold.py -q Pass: green; helpers imported from tests/test_scheduler.py (make_group, completing_executor) — that 66 KB file is not edited.
    • With a StubBroker-style broker and EscalationPolicy("on_stuck", "orchestrator_only"), the hold raises one driver_items_pending request whose group_id is g1 (the dependency) and whose prompt names g2 and g3 (both dependents) — not one request per dependent; a retry response releases both without writing driver-items.json; EscalationPolicy("on_failure", …) never raises it. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_driver_items_hold.py tests/test_escalation.py -q Pass: green, and test_escalation.py's tier tests name the new kind in on_stuck and interactive.

  • Edge cases: two dependents of one dependency share one escalation and one release file; a dependency whose items are all recorded before any dependent becomes admissible never raises a request; a RESOLVED dependency holds like a COMPLETED one
  • Non-goals / must-not: a group with no dependencies is never held; a dependency's skipped-recorded item does not hold; the hold never applies to a FAILED/INTERRUPTED dependency (those strand dependents as today). <!-- deepened 2026-10-10 from plan sha256:a8f26a9314dc -->

1"""A real two-group confined run held at a driver item (plan U2, live tier).
2
3**This tier spends real tokens.** Excluded from a plain `pytest` by
4`addopts = -m "not llm"`; opt in with `uv run pytest -m llm`.
5
6g1 is one line of code plus a required `Run (driver):` item the coder cannot
7run; g2 depends on it. The run is a subprocess so this test can act *during*
8it: wait for the hold line in `logs/run.log`, record the item from its own
9process, and watch g2 launch.
10"""
11

42"""

46 done = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
47 assert done.returncode == 0, f"git {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr}"
48 return done.stdout

52 g1 = Group(

54 name="farewell",
55 summary="Add a farewell function beside greet().",
56 spec=(
57 "In greeting.py, add a function `farewell()` returning the string "
58 '"goodbye", right after `greet()`. Then commit the change. '
59 "Do not change anything else."
60 ),
61 difficulty=0.1,
62 intensity=ReviewIntensity.SELF_VERIFY,
63 files=["greeting.py"],
64 verification=[
65 VerificationItem(
66 id="v1",
67 description="Run (driver): python -c 'import greeting' Pass: exits 0",
68 )
69 ],
70 )

72 id="g2",
73 name="note",
74 summary="Add a NOTES.md file.",
75 spec="Create NOTES.md containing the single line `done`. Commit it. Change nothing else.",
76 difficulty=0.1,
77 intensity=ReviewIntensity.SELF_VERIFY,
78 dependencies=["g1"],
79 files=["NOTES.md"],
80 verification=[VerificationItem(id="v2", description="NOTES.md exists")],
81 )
82 return [g1, g2]

86 repo = tmp_path / "live-repo-driver-hold"
87 repo.mkdir()
88 _git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
89 _git(repo, "config", "user.email", "live@test")
90 _git(repo, "config", "user.name", "live")
91 (repo / "README.md").write_text("# driver hold fixture\n")
92 (repo / "greeting.py").write_text('def greet():\n return "hello"\n')
93 (repo / "plan.md").write_text(
94 "# plan\n\n## Tasks\n\n- u1-farewell: add farewell()\n- u2-note: add NOTES.md\n"
95 )
96 _git(repo, "add", "-A")
97 _git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "init")
98 (repo / ".orchestrator").mkdir()
99 (repo / ".orchestrator" / "config.toml").write_text(_CONFIG_TOML)
100 grouping_dir = repo / ".orchestrator" / "groupings" / "plan"
101 grouping_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
102 (grouping_dir / "groups.json").write_text(
103 serialize_grouping(GroupingResult(plan_path="plan.md", groups=_groups()))
104 )
105 (grouping_dir / "base-context.md").write_text(
106 "A tiny scratch repo. Keep every change minimal.\n"
107 )

111def test_dependent_group_launches_only_after_the_driver_records_the_item(tmp_path):
112 repo = _build_repo(tmp_path)
113 paths = RunPaths(repo, RUN_ID)
114 log_path = paths.run_dir / "logs" / "run.log"
115 out = (tmp_path / "stdout.txt").open("w")
116 proc = subprocess.Popen(
117 [
118 sys.executable,
119 "-m",
120 "orchestrator.cli",
121 "run",
122 "--repo",
123 str(repo),
124 "--run-id",
125 RUN_ID,
126 "--intensity",
127 "autonomous",
128 ],
129 stdout=out,
130 stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
131 )
132 try:
133 deadline = time.monotonic() + RUN_TIMEOUT_S
134 held = "group g2: held — dependency g1"
135 while time.monotonic() < deadline:
136 if log_path.is_file() and held in log_path.read_text():
137 break
138 assert proc.poll() is None, f"run exited before holding g2: {proc.returncode}"
139 time.sleep(2)
140 else:
141 pytest.fail("g2 was never held on g1's driver item")
142
143 state = json.loads(paths.state_path.read_text())
144 assert state["groups"]["g1"]["state"] == "completed"
145 assert state["groups"]["g2"]["state"] == "pending"
146
147 record_driver_item(paths, _groups()[0], "v1", "pass", "recorded by the live test")
148 returncode = proc.wait(timeout=max(1.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
149 finally:
150 if proc.poll() is None:
151 proc.kill()
152 out.close()
153
154 assert returncode == 0, (tmp_path / "stdout.txt").read_text()
155 state = json.loads(paths.state_path.read_text())
156 assert state["groups"]["g1"]["state"] == "completed"
157 assert state["groups"]["g2"]["state"] == "completed"

g3: observatory-kind-mirror

u11: Adds `driver_items_pending` to the Observatory's escalation-kind union and label map and a test that fails whenever a Python `EscalationKind` value is missing from `ui/src/types.ts`, so the next new kind cannot drift silently.

Plan section U11

U11. observatory-kind-mirror — the Observatory lists driver_items_pending and a drift test pins every escalation kind to the UI union

  • Summary: Adds driver_items_pending to the Observatory's escalation-kind union and label map and a test that fails whenever a Python EscalationKind value is missing from ui/src/types.ts, so the next new kind cannot drift silently.
  • Goal: ui/src/types.ts lists "driver_items_pending" in the kind union and ui/src/components/EscalationPanel.tsx maps it to Driver items pending; tests/test_observatory_escalations.py gains a test that reads types.ts and asserts every EscalationKind value appears as a quoted literal in it.
  • Recipe: —
  • Files: ui/src/types.ts, ui/src/components/EscalationPanel.tsx, tests/test_observatory_escalations.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: U2
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • The drift test names a kind removed from types.ts and passes on the real file. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_observatory_escalations.py -q Pass: green.
    • External oracle: the UI compiles with the new literal and label. Run: npm --prefix ui run build Pass: exit 0.
  • Edge cases: —
  • Non-goals / must-not: no new UI behaviour beyond the label; hold reasons stay un-enumerated in the UI (the status subcommand already prints them).
Spec given to this group

Group g3: observatory-kind-mirror — mirror driver_items_pending into the Observatory and pin the kind→label map against drift

Members:

  • u11-observatory-kind-mirror

Intra-group order: single unit, no intra-group dependencies.

Upstream: g4 (u2-driver-items-hold) adds HoldReason.DRIVER_ITEMS and EscalationKind.DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING to orchestrator/model.py and raises the escalation from the scheduler. That Python-side change is not yours — orchestrator/model.py is outside this group's Files and must not be touched.

Downstream: g5 (u9-version-bump) bumps the plugin version once every unit, including this one, has merged.

Read unit U11 in the plan document for the authoritative Goal, Files, Edge cases and Non-goals; this spec only adds what the rewrite below changed.

Rewrite note — the drift guard already exists

This spec was rewritten mid-run after an upstream group reported an interface mismatch:

tests/test_observatory_model_drift.py::test_every_escalation_kind_is_known_to_the_ui[driver_items_pending] fails until ui/src/types.ts lists driver_items_pending (u11 / g3 work). Not edited there because the UI files are outside that group's Files.

So the repo already carries the generic drift guard U11 describes: tests/test_observatory_model_drift.py parametrises over EscalationKind (and GroupState, HumanAction, CoderReport.status) and asserts each value appears as a quoted literal in ui/src/types.ts. Do not re-implement that guard in tests/test_observatory_escalations.py — a second copy of the same assertion is duplication, and that file is in your Files only so you can add the one check the existing guard does not make.

What this group therefore does:

  1. ui/src/types.ts — add "driver_items_pending" to the escalation-kind string union, in the file's existing style and ordering. This is the edit that turns the failing parametrised case green.
  2. ui/src/components/EscalationPanel.tsx — add the label-map entry driver_items_pending: "Driver items pending". No other UI behaviour changes.
  3. tests/test_observatory_escalations.py — add one drift test that closes the gap the existing guard leaves: every EscalationKind value must have a label in EscalationPanel.tsx's label map, not merely a literal in the type union. Read the component source as text (the same cheap-source-read approach tests/test_observatory_model_drift.py uses for types.ts), parametrised or looped over EscalationKind, with an assertion message naming the missing kind. That way the next new kind cannot ship with a type literal and no human-readable label.

Constraints

  • Python enum, scheduler, hold reasons and CLI are out of scope. Hold reasons stay un-enumerated in the UI (the status subcommand already prints them verbatim) — do not add a hold-reason union.
  • If EscalationKind.DRIVER_ITEMS_PENDING is not yet present in orchestrator/model.py on your branch base (g4 may not have merged yet), the parametrised case for it simply does not exist. Add the types.ts literal and the label entry anyway — they are the mirror the upstream expects — and make your new label-map test pass over whatever kinds the enum currently has. Do not add the enum member to unblock yourself.
  • Keep the TypeScript idiomatic for the file: same quoting, same union formatting, same label-map shape as the neighbouring entries.

Done means

uv run pytest tests/test_observatory_model_drift.py tests/test_observatory_escalations.py -q is green, npm --prefix ui run build exits 0, and no file outside this group's Files is modified.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the plan digest: one summary line per unit) — never another group's spec.

g6: untracked-archive-first — the merge gate archives untracked leftovers on the first strike and merges; no relaunch unless the operator asks

u4: `_handle_untracked` escalates as today, then archives the untracked paths to `groups/<gid>/untracked/`, spreads the informational surprise and re-runs the gate on timeout, autonomous or `answer`; only `retry --text` relaunches, with a note that says `git mv … .coder-scratch/` and never "delete"; `_untracked_strikes` is removed from the ladder, the host and the flow doc.

Plan section U4

U4. untracked-archive-first — the merge gate archives untracked leftovers on the first strike and merges; no relaunch unless the operator asks

  • Summary: _handle_untracked escalates as today, then archives the untracked paths to groups/<gid>/untracked/, spreads the informational surprise and re-runs the gate on timeout, autonomous or answer; only retry --text relaunches, with a note that says git mv … .coder-scratch/ and never "delete"; _untracked_strikes is removed from the ladder, the host and the flow doc.
  • Goal: One strike, one outcome: the gate's untracked failure never costs a coder generation on its own. Before archiving, every untracked path that exactly matches an entry of the group's declared file list gets git added and committed as code(<gid>): commit declared file left untracked with the line group <gid>: committed N declared file(s) left untracked — <paths> (a coder's forgotten tests/test_x.py ships; a probe artifact with an undeclared name does not); only the remaining paths are archived. The run.log line UNTRACKED FILES ARCHIVED — moved to <archive>: <paths>; merging is logged once per merge, the surprise names the archive, and the coder-facing note (relaunch-with-text only) reads untracked files left in the worktree: <paths> — commit them or git mv them into .coder-scratch/. merge_ladder.py:69, host.py:53, review.py:184 and docs/orchestrator-flow.md:74 drop _untracked_strikes.

    • Nothing else in the ladder changed. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_merge_gate_triage.py tests/test_review_loop.py -q Pass: green.

g8: report-commit-pointers — one-pager pointers accept every commit in the run's range

u7: `GitRangeFacts` carries `commits` (8-character prefixes of `git rev-list base..tip` plus `base`, oldest first) and `_valid_pointers` accepts them, so a scaffold written before the one-pager commit still validates after it.

Plan section U7

U7. report-commit-pointers — one-pager pointers accept every commit in the run's range

  • Summary: GitRangeFacts carries commits (8-character prefixes of git rev-list base..tip plus base, oldest first) and _valid_pointers accepts them, so a scaffold written before the one-pager commit still validates after it.
  • Goal: _resolve_git_range fills commits when the range is available (empty list otherwise); _valid_pointers adds every entry; the scaffold's valid pointers comment lists them. facts.json round-trips the field.
  • Recipe: —
  • Files: orchestrator/report/facts.py, orchestrator/report/onepager.py, tests/test_report_onepager.py, tests/test_report_facts.py
  • Symbols: —
  • Depends-on: —
  • Slice: —
  • Implements / Consumes: —
  • Verification:
    • A bullet pointing at an intermediate commit's 8-char prefix validates; one pointing at a sha outside the range is still unknown pointer. Run: uv run pytest tests/test_report_onepager.py -q Pass: green.
    • External oracle: on a tmp git repo with three commits on an integration branch, build_facts yields commits of length 3 (base plus two). Run: uv run pytest tests/test_report_facts.py -q -k commits Pass: green.
  • Edge cases: —
  • Non-goals / must-not: no change to the one-pager's word/bullet rules.
