Plan section U8

U8. run-skill-and-docs — the run-driver skill, the flow doc and the glossary describe the new hold, record, data step, untracked outcome and failure default

  • Summary: Rewrites the run-driver skill's affected rows and phases (Monitor rule for a timed-out request, the untracked row, driver-item and data-step usage, --on-failure guidance, the held — dependency anchor), adds driver-item and data-step to docs/orchestrator-flow.md §7, and adds Driver Item Record and Data Step to CONTEXT.md while correcting Failure Policy.
  • Goal: A driver following the skill text alone runs every Run (driver): item from the integration worktree at a tip that includes the dependency's merge (never from the main checkout or the group's own worktree), records the outcome with driver-item the moment the command returns (skipped with the reason when an item is moot, e.g. a RESOLVED group's), and knows a held — dependency line means dependents are waiting on exactly that record; runs every data-writing step through data-step, reads a request file with no response as "answered, timed out, or pending — the status subcommand is the truth" (the Phase 2 Monitor condition (a) names the ESCALATION <id> timed out line), runs every data-writing step through data-step from the integration worktree and expects a long one to hold every merge for its whole duration, and knows a halted run only arises from --on-failure halt. The preflight_failed table row no longer promises a relaunch. The anchors table gains group <gid>: held — dependency <dep> …, driver item <id> recorded, data step started/finished, gate waiting for driver data step, UNTRACKED FILES ARCHIVED, harness pin reset by retry. triage-guide.md is checked for the same claims and corrected where it repeats them. CONTEXT.md entries follow the file's **Term**: / _Avoid_: form.

422**Driver Item Record**:
423The run's own memory of which `Run (driver):` verification items the run driver
424has executed, kept in `groups/<gid>/driver-items.json` and written by the
425`driver-item` subcommand. The scheduler holds dependents of a group whose items
426are unrecorded, and auto-finish waits on the same record.
427_Avoid_: driver log (a log is not read back), sign-off (nobody approves; the
428record is evidence)
429
430**Data Step**:
431A driver command that writes the shared data layer (`[workspace] data_dirs`),
432run through `data-step` so it holds the run's `data-step.lock` and no merge gate
433reads the data while it writes. A long one holds every merge for its duration.
434_Avoid_: ingest (one kind of data step), driver item (a verification, not a write)

g5: harness-pin-on-success-and-version-bump

u3: `EvaluateExecution` and `OptimizeExecution` compare against `run/eval/harness.sha256` when it exists but write it only once the smoke and the first scoring command exit 0, and `retry_group` deletes the pin logging the old combined hash — so a fixture fixed after a failed smoke passes `retry`, while a harness edited under a running loop still fails naming the path.

Plan section U3

U3. harness-pin-on-success — evaluate/optimize pin the harness hash only after a successful smoke and first scoring; retry resets the pin

  • Summary: EvaluateExecution and OptimizeExecution compare against run/eval/harness.sha256 when it exists but write it only once the smoke and the first scoring command exit 0, and retry_group deletes the pin logging the old combined hash — so a fixture fixed after a failed smoke passes retry, while a harness edited under a running loop still fails naming the path.
  • Goal: In evaluate_executor.py, _before_commands keeps the compare-or-fail branch, computes the snapshot, runs the smoke, and defers the write to a new _pin_harness(snapshot) called from _after_measurements (first successful scoring) when no pin exists; the record's harness_hash is unchanged. In optimize_executor.py, _run_evaluation writes the pin at its end, after the measurements are read, when absent. _retry_failed in retry.py removes <group_dir>/run/eval/harness.sha256 if present and logs group <gid>: harness pin reset by retry (was <combined[:12]>). docs/orchestrator-kpi-harness.md replaces "hashed once, at first use" with the new rule and names retry as the reset.

Spec given to this group

Group g5 — harness-pin-on-success (U3) + version-bump (U9)

Implement units U3 (harness-pin-on-success) and U9 (version-bump) exactly as specified in the plan document you have as shared context (docs/plans/2026-10-10-001-fix-run-r20261007-100412-seams-plan.md, §Units U3 and U9) and under the plan's Decisions section ("The harness hash is pinned only after the smoke and the first scoring exit 0, and retry deletes the pin"). Do not restate the plan; follow it.

Intra-group order

  1. u3-harness-pin-on-success — the whole behavioural change.
  2. u9-version-bump — .claude-plugin/plugin.json 0.22.1 → 0.23.0, in its own one-file commit with a chore(plugin): 0.23.0 — … subject and nothing else in the diff. U9 depends on every other unit of the plan having merged; your group is the last one, so make the bump the final commit on your branch. pyproject.toml's version stays 0.1.0.

Spec refinement from a mid-run surprise (binding)

This spec was refined mid-run in light of a surprise reported by another group: the documentation group (g9, U8) found that no harness pin reset by retry log line exists anywhere in orchestrator/execution/retry.py on this branch — the run-driver skill's log-anchor row it is adding assumes this group emits that text. That is correct and expected: U3 is the unit that introduces it, and retry.py today logs only group <gid>: retried by operator — refreshed onto <integration>, reset to pending (retry.py:140).

Treat the log text as a cross-group contract you own. In _retry_failed (orchestrator/execution/retry.py:110), when <group_dir>/run/eval/harness.sha256 exists, delete it and log, verbatim and character-for-character:

group <gid>: harness pin reset by retry (was <combined[:12]>)

where <combined[:12]> is the first 12 characters of the combined hash read from the pin file before deletion. Emit it through the same logging path as the existing retried by operator line so it lands in logs/run.log (that is what the skill anchor and the live test grep). When no pin exists, log nothing extra — the retry path must be byte-identical to today's for non-evaluate groups. Do not rename, reword, re-case or re-order this message; g9's anchors table and docs/orchestrator-kpi-harness.md both point at it.

What to implement (U3)

  • orchestrator/execution/evaluate_executor.py: _before_commands keeps its compare-or-fail branch (an existing pin that disagrees with the current snapshot still raises GroupFailure("… harness path changed since the first evaluation: <path>"), naming the path) and still computes the snapshot and runs the smoke — but no longer writes the pin. The write moves to a new _pin_harness(snapshot) called from _after_measurements, i.e. after the first scoring command exits 0, and only when no pin file exists. The record's harness_hash field is unchanged.
  • orchestrator/execution/optimize_executor.py: _run_evaluation keeps the compare-or-fail branch and writes the pin at its end, after the measurements are read, when absent.
  • orchestrator/execution/retry.py: the pin reset above.
  • docs/orchestrator-kpi-harness.md:41-43: replace "hashed once, at first use" with the new rule (compared whenever present, written once the smoke and the first scoring exit 0) and name retry as the reset.

The point of the pin is to catch a harness edited under a running loop; a failed smoke scored nothing, so there is nothing to protect, and retry is the operator's explicit "I changed the world". Both halves are needed: pin-on-success alone still fails a retry after a successful first attempt, and retry-reset alone leaves a stale pin after a crash re-entry.

Tests

tests/test_evaluate_recipe.py's test_editing_harness_between_attempts_fails_the_second_attempt_naming_it (line 152) pins today's behaviour — re-shape it, do not delete it: an edit after a successful first attempt must still fail naming scripts/score.sh. Add the new cases to tests/test_evaluate_recipe.py, tests/test_optimize_executor.py and tests/test_retry.py using those files' existing fixtures (repo, make_group, make_deps, _run, base_args / the setup-style helpers). The live-tier file tests/test_harness_pin_live.py is new and yours alone: pytestmark = [pytest.mark.llm, skipif(no claude)], modelled on tests/test_run_recipe_live.py, driving python -m orchestrator.cli for retry and resume. It is run by the driver, not by you.

Done means

Every verification item below passes; uv run pytest -q is green (the -m llm file is excluded by addopts); the mutable-region check is untouched (test_candidate_editing_harness_is_a_mutable_violation_and_discarded stays green); the harness pin reset by retry (was …) text exists verbatim in retry.py; and plugin.json reads 0.23.0 in a final one-file commit.

Before this spec the workers read only the shared context (base-context.md, with the plan digest: one summary line per unit) — never another group's spec.

53def _cli(repo: Path, *argv: str, expected_exit: int | None = 0) -> str:
54 done = subprocess.run(
55 [sys.executable, "-m", "orchestrator.cli", *argv],
56 cwd=repo,
57 capture_output=True,
58 text=True,
59 timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT_S,
60 )
61 if expected_exit is not None:
62 assert done.returncode == expected_exit, (
63 f"{argv[0]} exited {done.returncode}\n{done.stdout}\n{done.stderr}"
64 )
65 return done.stdout + done.stderr
66

Group cost

GroupSessionsTokensCache-read tokens
g1: driver-item-record — the Driver Item Record: `record_driver_item` writes an item's outcome, auto-finish reads it, and a run group's own command satisfies a prefix-matching item + data-step-lock — the gate and driver data steps exclude each other through `data-step.lock`, held by the gate and by `run_data_step` 2 215,279 2,408,047
g2: cli-subcommands — `driver-item` and `data-step` on the CLI, the status subcommand's driver-item lines, and the launch-time data-layer warning 1 113,080 3,202,643
g4: driver-items-hold — the scheduler holds a dependent group while a dependency carries unrecorded driver items, and tells the driver how to release it 1 119,436 1,752,783
g3: observatory-kind-mirror 1 59,478 288,585
g6: untracked-archive-first — the merge gate archives untracked leftovers on the first strike and merges; no relaunch unless the operator asks 1 95,389 867,188
g7: overlap-default — `on_group_failure` defaults to `overlap` 1 67,717 446,626
g8: report-commit-pointers — one-pager pointers accept every commit in the run's range 1 75,464 765,273
g9: run-skill-and-docs — the run-driver skill, the flow doc and the glossary describe the new hold, record, data step, untracked outcome and failure default 1 82,052 900,460
g5: harness-pin-on-success-and-version-bump 4 316,460 4,667,047

Tokens = input + output + cache-creation. Cache reads are billed separately and listed apart so a warm session does not inflate the headline.
